=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: PR description states the audit "fix[es] stale facts" and "the template copies are changed where they are identical or have the same wording"; the live copy of `.claude/commands/apply-url.md` was changed in four hunks (the same context-loading wording as the other updated commands, plus the "to hand it to the orchestrator" wording) but the matching template copy was not, leaving the audit deliverable half-applied for apply-url.
  Expected change site: `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/apply-url.md`
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff contains zero hunks for `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/apply-url.md`. The CI check `test_live_copies_match_their_templates` fails with the message `Live .claude/ copies differ from workflow-templates/.claude/ for: commands/apply-url.md`, which cascades from the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job to the aggregate `lint` job and blocks merge. The file is not listed in `.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json` (verified: that file only carries `analyze-log`, `deploy-activate`, `implement-issue-claude`, `investigate-issue`, `validate-consumer-issue`, `verify-activation` — `apply-url.md` is not among them, so the parity test requires byte-identical copies). The autofix commit (59c65f0) merged in `603dbd1` was scoped to "audit-plans, implement-plan-ai and write-plan" (per its own message) and never extended to apply-url. The new regression test `test_command_context_reads_follow_claude_md` includes apply-url in its live target list but not in its template target list — a tell that the test author recognised the template gap and worked around it instead of fixing it. The changelog fragment lists apply-url in the "Commands changed" row but not in the "Template copies changed" row, so the changelog is internally inconsistent with the actual diff and would ship misleading release notes.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The regression test `test_command_context_reads_follow_claude_md` should enforce the new context-loading pattern in both the live and template copies of every command the audit touched, so a future PR that updates one side but not the other fails CI before merge.
  Expected change site: `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py` lines 31-46 (the `targets` list in `test_command_context_reads_follow_claude_md`)
  Evidence of absence: The live target list is `("apply-analysis", "apply-url", "audit-plans", "implement-plan-ai", "validate-consumer-issue", "write-plan")` but the template target list is `("apply-analysis", "audit-plans", "implement-plan-ai", "write-plan")` — apply-url and validate-consumer-issue are live-only. validate-consumer-issue is allowlisted in `.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json` so its omission from the template list is correct; apply-url is not allowlisted there, so its omission is the exact gap that lets the parity failure slip past this test. The same omission is what would let a future PR reintroduce the old full-read instruction in `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/apply-url.md` without this regression catching it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The changelog fragment should accurately list every file the PR changes, so consumers and contributors reading release notes can audit the diff.
  Expected change site: `changelog.d/6435-prompt-audit-claude-config.md` (the "Template copies changed" row in the metrics table)
  Evidence of absence: The "Commands changed" row lists `apply-url` among eleven commands; the "Template copies changed" row lists `{apply-analysis,audit-plans,deploy-activate,implement-plan-ai,verify-activation,write-plan}.md` and omits `apply-url`. If the template is later updated to match the live copy (the BLOCKER fix), the changelog's "Template copies changed" row must be updated in the same PR so the assembled `CHANGELOG.md` correctly credits the work; if the template is instead left divergent, the changelog currently misrepresents the deliverable. Either way, the row is wrong on the current PR head.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
